standard_prerequisites.name: Compatibility of the cycle class map with pushforwards along a finite morphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Axiom (C) on the compatibility of the cycle class map with proper pushforwards, and the lemma relating the classes of points of the same degree
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the equality of cycle classes from the base change back to the original scheme.

core_obligations: Reduce to two points (proof lines 3703-3707): by generation of the group of zero cycles by points with separable residue fields it suffices to show that for two such points the product of the degree of one with the cycle class of the other agrees in the other order.

Reduce to rational points (proof lines 3709-3722): choosing a finite Galois extension containing the residue fields of the two points and base changing, the two points lift to rational points of the base change whose pushforwards are the original points scaled by the degrees of the residue field extensions; compatibility of the cycle class map with pushforwards reduces the comparison to rational points.

Conclude for rational points (proof lines 3724-3734): for rational points, the difference becomes divisible by an integer larger than one after a suitable finite separable extension, and the relations lemma shows that the cycle classes of the two lifted points agree; compatibility with pushforwards gives the equality downstairs, which finishes the proof.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to closed points with separable residue fields.
Base change along a finite Galois extension to obtain rational points.
Use divisibility of the difference and the relations lemma to compare the classes.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a geometrically irreducible smooth projective scheme over a finite separable extension the cycle class map on zero cycles factors through the degree map (statement lines 3696-3703). The proof (proof lines 3704-3734) reduces to points with separable residue fields, base changes along a finite Galois extension to reach rational points, and uses divisibility of the difference together with the relations lemma. H3: a three stage reduction using base change and divisibility, written out in full.
